text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres concerned that about half of the MPs of the ruling Socialist Party have so far not adopted a position on abortion, the newspaper learned.
- Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco will go on the offensive against northern European states if their politicians make statements to destabilise "Club Med" economies, the newspaper learned.
- Productivity of state airline TAP-Air Portugal is 30 percent below the European average, according to a study by the European Association of Airlines.
- The government approved a resolution that sets general terms for the revision of the restructuring plan of ship repairer Lisnave.

- European Commission warned in a report published in Brussels yesterday that the deterioration of Portugal's labour market, growing social security costs and the need to invest in education and infrastructure threatened budgetary consolidation.
- The ruling Socialist Party and opposition Social Democratic Party are united in their determination that Portugal should join the first wave of Economic and Monetary Union in 1999.
- Striking Spanish truck drivers step up pressure on the government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar. Portuguese truckers and road transport companies begin to count their losses.
